correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the oriented top-boundary Gram matrix B^T B=mI-ss^T, rank m-1 and unique relation sum s_i v_i=0. Even m=2k yields the orthogonal free sum of two centered regular (k-1)-simplices, dimension m-2; facets indexed by A x B, each normal has squared norm (m-2)/(2m), giving unique inradius sqrt(2m/(m-2)) and circumradius sqrt(m(m-2)). Symmetry and irreducibility yield spherical John and Loewner shapes. Odd m=2k+1: s-sum epsilon is nonzero, so simplex dimension m-1; barycentric normal g_i=(e_i-epsilon*s_i*1)/m has lengths sqrt(m-1)/m (majority) and sqrt(m+3)/m (minority). Summed facet inequalities give unique inradius 2m/[(m+1)sqrt(m-1)+(m-1)sqrt(m+3)]. Averaging the majority vertices proves the unique enclosing sphere radius m*sqrt((m-1)/(m+1)), with strict minority squared clearance 4m/(m+1). Restricted linear map L on 1-perp has singular values 1 and m (multiplicities 1,m-2), giving displayed anisotropic John/Loewner semiaxes and common center c_J. Independently reconstructed L, affine ranks, SVD singular axes, odd screen clearance, and even circumradius numerically m=3..15 in local standalone check; not an infinite proof.
